title: Caching (the two hard things in computer science)
description:
Byte caches everything. Compy asks what happens when the data changes. A short tour of cache invalidation.

#caching #webdev #programming #shorts
angle: Caching makes things fast by remembering answers, and the hard part is knowing when a remembered answer has gone stale.
hook: There's an old joke that computer science has two hard problems. One of them is today's topic.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: There's an old joke that computer science has two hard problems. One of them is today's topic.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Naming things and cache invalidation. Today: why the second one earns its place.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: A cache keeps a copy of an answer close by, so you skip the slow trip to get it again.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: I am basically a cache. I remember where I left my charger.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: A miss means a slow trip, then you save the answer.

props.code:
def get(key):
    if key in cache: return cache[key]
    value = slow_lookup(key)
    cache[key] = value
    return value

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Great. So we cache everything and go home early.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Your profile photo changes. The cache still shows the old one. Nobody told it.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Right, so we need to know when to throw the copy away.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Common fix: give each copy a lifetime. When it expires, the next request fetches fresh data.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: The tradeoff is speed against freshness. You pick how stale is acceptable.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Rule of the day: a cache is a bet that the answer hasn't changed.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Follow for more. Next: why 404 means not found, and 418 means teapot.

claims.text: The saying 'two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation and naming things' is attributed to Phil Karlton
HTTP Cache-Control max-age sets how long a response is considered fresh
A cache stores copies of data so future requests can be served faster
